tests_notes: Integer and float series, window of one, full-length window, short series, invalid windows; workload: 5000 floats with a window of 200.

A.rationale: Each step re-slices and re-sums the whole window, O(n·w). Keeping a running total and adding the entering value minus the leaving one is O(n); results agree to rounding error.

B.rationale: accumulate builds all prefix sums in one C-level pass; each window sum is then one subtraction. Same length, same ValueError, and the means match to floating-point rounding.

C.strategy: List comprehension instead of append loop
C.rationale: Conservative micro-optimization: a comprehension avoids the per-item append call. The slicing and summing are untouched, so every value is bit-for-bit identical.

notes: Floats: A and B change the summation order, so tests use pytest.approx and the differential check's 1e-9 relative tolerance accepts them. C keeps the O(n·w) work and measures as no change.
